findings.title: footgun: createCycleCostCondition carries a token form `self.state.<resource>.value >= amountRef`, i.e. the has-enough-resource check reads as a plain >= on the raw resource value.
findings.detail: The runtime evaluator (JsonLogicAdapter.evaluate) uses rule.compiled when present and only compiles from tokens as a fallback, so the authoritative predicate is the compiled `>` on `(resource.value + 1)` vs amountRef (a +1 grace unit), not the token's `>=`. The tokens are dead for evaluation and encode a different boundary; editing the visible token `>=` has zero runtime effect.

adjudication.notes: The condition object carries both `tokens` (>= on raw value) and a `compiled` (> on value+1); JsonLogicAdapter.evaluate uses rule.compiled when present and only compiles tokens as fallback, so the tokens are dead and disagree with the runtime boundary. Genuine maintainer footgun, but cannot itself change behavior since compiled is authoritative.

findings.title: footgun: createCycleCostPowerGateRule's condition token form is `self.state.<resource>.value < amountRef` (gate power when resource is below the cost).
findings.detail: The compiled form actually evaluated is `(resource.value + 1) <= amountRef` (a +1 grace unit and a <= boundary), so the token `<` is dead and disagrees with the runtime boundary; a maintainer reading or editing the tokens sees the wrong predicate.

adjudication.notes: Same pattern as .004: the power-gate condition's tokens say `<` while the present `compiled` says `<=` on (value+1); compiled wins at runtime, so the visible `<` token is dead and misleading. Footgun, not a runtime defect.

findings.title: footgun: createCycleRule's is_active gate condition is `{ t: 'ref', v: 'self.state.cycle_active' }`, reading like a boolean check that the cycle is active (cycle_active is a state entry `{value:1|0}`).
findings.detail: The ref omits `.value`, so it compiles to `{var:'self.state.cycle_active'}` which json-logic-js resolves to the whole state-entry OBJECT (not its numeric value). A non-null object is always truthy, so this gate is truthy even when cycle_active.value is 0; every other compiled condition in the subsystem uses the `.value` suffix. The intended gating is effectively inert here (masked only because conditional-activation also zeroes powerSink.throttle, which zeroes the accumulated allocatedDraw*dt_s).

adjudication.notes: The is_active condition has NO compiled field, just a single ref token `self.state.cycle_active` (no `.value`); compileExpression turns it into `{var:'self.state.cycle_active'}`, which json-logic resolves to the whole state-entry object (truthy even when value is 0). The gate is effectively inert; every sibling condition uses the `.value` suffix. Live latent bug, masked only by conditional-activation zeroing throttle.

findings.title: footgun: config.maxSubSteps (schema-capped at 16) reads as the ceiling on physics substeps per tick.

findings.title: footgun: computeObstacleAvoidance takes a general 'neighbors' list and is fed the full spatial query buffer, reading as if it avoids all nearby bodies.
findings.detail: 'if (!neighbor.isStatic) continue;' skips every dynamic body, so only STATIC bodies are ever treated as obstacles; dynamic bodies are never avoided by this path (they rely on separation instead).

adjudication.notes: Line 89 'if (!neighbor.isStatic) continue;' confirmed inside findClosestObstacle; the buffer passed in (ImpulseSteeringForces.ts:42-49) is the full spatial query, yet only static bodies are ever considered obstacles. Dynamic bodies are handled by computeSeparation instead. Accurate name-vs-behavior footgun; behavior itself is by-design, so low.

findings.title: footgun: queryRadius is documented as returning 'all bodies that *might* collide with the given circle (x, y, radius)'.
findings.detail: It queries a square (half-extent=radius, not a circle) and its containment test only checks each neighbor's CENTER against that box, ignoring the neighbor's own radius, so a large body straddling the query circle from just outside can be missed; it is not collision-complete.

adjudication.notes: queryRadius (line 230) doc says 'all bodies that *might* collide with the given circle', but it delegates to queryRaw with half-extent=radius (a square) and queryRaw (lines 199-208) tests only each neighbor's center against the box, ignoring neighbor radius. A large body whose center sits just outside the box but whose disc overlaps the query circle is missed; not collision-complete. Real edge-case gap, low.

findings.title: footgun: applySeek is exported as part of the steering API, implying it is a live force applied during ticks.
findings.detail: applySeek has zero callers anywhere in src (only computeSeek is used); it is dead exported code.

adjudication.notes: applySeek defined at Steering.ts:35; grep -rn 'applySeek' src/ returns only the definition, no callers. computeSeek is the live path. Dead exported code that reads as a live force API. Real footgun, low (cannot affect runtime, purely maintainability).

findings.title: footgun: applySeparation is exported alongside computeSeparation and takes a Quadtree, implying it is the live separation entry point.
findings.detail: applySeparation has zero callers in src; the live path is computeSeparation via ImpulseSteeringForces, and this quadtree-based wrapper is dead code.

adjudication.notes: applySeparation (quadtree-taking wrapper) defined at ImpulseSeparation.ts:56; grep -rn 'applySeparation' src/ returns only the definition, no callers. Live separation path is computeSeparation via ImpulseSteeringForces.ts:53. Dead exported code presenting as the entry point. Real footgun, low.

findings.title: footgun: ENTITY_ID_PATTERN plus the broken-reference machinery reads as a general 'detect references to missing blueprints' check.
findings.detail: The pattern /\bentity_[a-z0-9]+\b/i only recognizes ids of the shape entity_<alnum>. Real blueprint/draftOption ids in src/data are nanoid-style (e.g. 0HNjKctJ5pN7Zwr6gV2ay) or human slugs (e.g. Accountant, 30_seconds_in) — 0 of 265 distinct ids are entity_-prefixed — so a missing reference to a real id never becomes a BrokenReference; broken detection fires only for the synthetic entity_ ids used in tests.

adjudication.notes: walk.ts:3 defines /\bentity_[a-z0-9]+\b/i and line 52 only pushes to broken when a value matches it; real module ids in src/data/raw are slugs (butcher, newbody) and nanoids (ztVe0xjtZLd1ph5twD3mV, 0HNjKctJ5pN7Zwr6gV2ay), none entity_-prefixed, and the tests use synthetic entity_* ids. Broken detection genuinely only fires for test-shaped ids; medium because the only consumer is a devtools issues panel, not a data gate.

findings.title: footgun: ENTITY_ID_PATTERN.test(value) reads as 'this string IS an entity id', so the recorded missingId is the referenced id.
findings.detail: test() is a substring match anchored only by \b word boundaries, not ^...$, so any free-text string that merely contains an entity_ token (e.g. 'spawn entity_foo now') matches, and broken.push records missingId: value = the entire string, not the matched id. The later filter existingIds.has(b.missingId) then compares that whole sentence against the id set.

adjudication.notes: The pattern at line 3 is anchored only by \b (no ^...$), so test() is a substring match, and lines 53-59 push missingId: value (the whole string); the filter in referenceIndex.ts:65 then checks existingIds.has on that whole string. Code-accurate, but only manifests for free-text containing an entity_ token, which does not occur in real data, so impact is narrow.

findings.title: footgun: existingIds.has(value) paired with a case-insensitive ENTITY_ID_PATTERN suggests id resolution is case-tolerant.
findings.detail: existingIds is a Set with exact case-sensitive lookup, while ENTITY_ID_PATTERN carries the i flag. A reference written as entity_A when the blueprint key is entity_a fails existingIds.has (miss), then matches the pattern, and is reported as a broken reference even though a case-variant of the target exists.

adjudication.notes: existingIds.has(value) at line 41 is a case-sensitive JS Set lookup while ENTITY_ID_PATTERN carries the i flag, so a case-variant reference (entity_A vs key entity_a) misses the Set, matches the pattern, and is reported broken. The sequence holds against the code, but only affects entity_-prefixed ids that exist solely in tests, so it is real but very narrow.

findings.title: footgun: applyStatePatch on a handler whose class comment and payload name (PATCH_BLUEPRINT, 'patches live entities') imply patching updates component values on existing entities.
findings.detail: For the 'state' component it ADDS only keys the live entity does not already have (line 19: `if (state[key] !== undefined) continue`); a patched value for an EXISTING state key is silently dropped on live entities even though the blueprint definition itself is updated. The test asserts hp stays 10 after a patch to 1 (PatchBlueprintHandler.test.ts:127).

adjudication.notes: applyStatePatch line 19 `if (state[key] !== undefined) continue` skips keys the live entity already has, so a patched value for an existing state key is silently dropped on live entities while the blueprint definition is updated; PatchBlueprintHandler.test.ts pins hp staying 10 after a patch to 1.

findings.title: footgun: The `total <= 0` guard logs `Transfer failed: target '<id>' at capacity.`, presenting a zero total as a target-capacity condition.
findings.detail: `total` is the sum of `result.clampedPayload`, which calculateTransaction clamps to BOTH target capacity AND source availability (transferLogic.ts clampToAvailable). A total of 0 also occurs when the source has nothing to send, so the 'at capacity' message misattributes a source-empty (or all-non-positive) transfer to the target being full.

adjudication.notes: total is the sum of finalPayload (clampToAvailable in transferLogic.ts), so a source with nothing to send also yields total===0, yet the guard logs "target '<id>' at capacity", misattributing a source-empty transfer to target fullness. Message-only, no state corruption.

findings.title: footgun: clampPayloadToCapacity is named as if it constrains a transfer payload to the target's remaining capacity.
findings.detail: Only positive, finite amounts are clamped; a non-finite or non-positive amount is copied into the output UNCHANGED (lines 53-55), so a negative or NaN transfer amount bypasses capacity clamping entirely and flows downstream.

adjudication.notes: Lines 53-55 do copy non-finite/non-positive amounts through unchanged, but the downstream transfer path (validateSourceEntry in transferLogic.ts) rejects amount<=0, so such values cannot actually flow through a transfer; the 'bypasses clamping and flows downstream' consequence does not hold.

findings.title: footgun: The `prefix` parameter (default "spawn", e.g. "pending") looks like it namespaces the id counter per prefix.
findings.detail: The serial is shared across all prefixes via the single sys_world.state.spawnSerial counter; the prefix is only a cosmetic label. Two different prefixes never produce the same numeric serial, but the counter does not restart per prefix (documented in the doc comment, contradicting the per-namespace impression the parameter gives).

adjudication.notes: The shared-serial behavior is exactly what the doc comment (lines 36-37) states; ids remain globally unique and per-prefix restart was never promised, so this is an immaterial naming observation, not a defect.

findings.title: footgun: The comment 'Mutate in-place so concurrent systems in the same tick see the update' plus the enqueued UPDATE_TRAITS_BATCH command frame this as merely enqueuing a state change, and Snapshot.getEntities() is typed ReadonlyArray<Readonly<RuntimeEntity>>.
findings.detail: executeAddTraitAction/executeRemoveTraitAction cast the readonly snapshot entity to a mutable type and directly push/splice context.self.traits (and even assign self.traits=[] when absent), mutating the live entity object during the read-only behavior phase. The Readonly typing is compile-time only; the entity is aliased into the snapshot, so behavior emits a side effect before its command is applied, unlike every other executor which only enqueues.

adjudication.notes: Snapshot.reset (Snapshot.ts:33) aliases the live entity array via a cast, not a clone, and getEntities() returns Readonly only at compile time; executeAddTraitAction/executeRemoveTraitAction cast self and push/splice/assign self.traits directly, mutating the live entity during the read-only behavior phase, unlike sibling executors that only enqueue.

findings.title: footgun: The name resolveContention and the ContentionRule framing suggest it only reorders transfer requests that compete for the same target resource.
findings.detail: It returns [...otherCommands, ...sortedTransfers], globally hoisting EVERY non-transfer command (KILL, SPAWN, MUTATE-derived, etc.) ahead of ALL transfer commands whenever the batch contains at least one transfer (see caller runtimeCollectCommands.ts line 20). Relative order between a non-transfer command and a transfer that preceded it in emission order is silently inverted.

adjudication.notes: resolveContention returns [...otherCommands, ...sortedTransfers], and the caller runtimeCollectCommands.ts:20 invokes it whenever any TRANSFER_ASSETS is present, so every non-transfer command is globally hoisted ahead of all transfers, inverting relative emission order between a non-transfer command and any transfer that preceded it.

findings.title: footgun: getAutomationComponent's comment says 'We trust the data is valid because it was validated on Spawn/Input' and returns the raw object typed as AutomationComponent, implying schema invariants (AutomationComponentSchema enforces intervalMs>=1) hold.
findings.detail: It only checks typeof === 'object' and casts via `as any`; no Zod parse runs. Any code path that writes an automation component with intervalMs of 0 (or a non-integer/negative repeats) is accepted, and resolveNextTiming then computes nextRemaining % 0 = NaN before falling back to intervalMs (0).

adjudication.notes: getAutomationComponent only checks typeof==='object' and casts via `as any`, no Zod parse; AutomationComponentSchema.intervalMs.min(1) is thus not enforced at read time, and with intervalMs=0 resolveNextTiming computes nextRemaining % 0 = NaN then falls back to intervalMs=0 (lines 81-85).

findings.title: footgun: applyOperator implements '/' as a normal division operator.
findings.detail: Division by zero returns 0 rather than Infinity/NaN, so an expression like `x / y` silently yields 0 when y resolves to 0 instead of surfacing the degenerate case; downstream mutations treat that 0 as a real computed value.

adjudication.notes: Line 17 returns 0 for division by zero rather than Infinity/NaN, so `x / 0` silently yields 0 and downstream mutations consume that 0 as a real computed value with no signal of the degenerate case.

findings.title: footgun: step() reads as a manual single-frame advance (a public sibling of start/stop that pushes the sim forward one step).
findings.detail: It invokes the callback with dt=0. The wired runtime callback (ui/runtime/state/runtimeFactory) forwards that to runtime.tick(0), and advanceRuntimeCoreTick treats dt<=0 as a no-op (normalizeDt(0)=0 -> returns null), so Ticker.step() advances nothing. The real single-step is RuntimeCore.stepOncePreservingPause(), which passes LOGIC_STEP_MS.

adjudication.notes: step() calls callback(0); runtimeFactory.ts:64-65 wires the callback to runtime.tick(dt), and advanceRuntimeCoreTick returns null when normalizeDt(0)<=0, so Ticker.step() advances nothing. The real single-step is RuntimeCore.stepOncePreservingPause() which passes LOGIC_STEP_MS.

findings.title: footgun: The docstring says "Resets ECS + physics state so game.init can re-spawn a fresh world", implying a full clean-slate reset.
findings.detail: It resets tick to 0 but never touches state.status. A runtime that went "fatal" stays fatal across reset(): RuntimeCore.reset() then calls pause(), which is guarded by status !== "fatal" and so no-ops. Only destroy() clears fatal (to "idle"). Reset does not recover a wedged runtime.

adjudication.notes: resetRuntimeState sets state.tick=0 but never state.status; RuntimeCore.reset() then calls pause(), which is guarded `if (status !== "fatal")` (RuntimeCoreBase.ts:74), so a fatal runtime stays fatal across reset(). Only destroy() clears it to 'idle' (runtimeCoreState.ts:31).

findings.title: footgun: advanceRuntimeCoreTick's parameter type RuntimeCoreTickState declares entityStore/systemPhaseBuffers/systemsRegistry as plain `object`, suggesting the type constrains what is passed.
findings.detail: Those fields are immediately cast to `never` before use (core.entityStore as never, etc.), so the declared `object` type provides no checking; the real contract is whatever tickRuntimeCore requires, enforced nowhere at this boundary.

adjudication.notes: entityStore/systemPhaseBuffers/systemsRegistry are typed `object` then cast to `never` at use (lines 52,55,56), so the declared type provides no checking. True but purely a compile-time typing observation with no runtime effect.

findings.title: footgun: SaveGameState.timeScale:number is a required field, implying the runtime's time scale is captured and restored across a save/load cycle.
findings.detail: The value is never derived from the live runtime and never read on load. serialize() writes a hardcoded 1 (RuntimeSerializer.ts:40) regardless of the actual RuntimeAccessors timeScale, and hydrateRuntime() never restores it. The field is inert on both ends.

adjudication.notes: serialize() writes a hardcoded `timeScale: 1` (RuntimeSerializer.ts:40) regardless of the live time scale, and hydrateRuntime() never reads timeScale, so the required SaveGameState.timeScale field is inert on both ends and does not round-trip.

findings.title: footgun: SaveGameState.systems.automation:AutomationSnapshot advertises that automation-system state is part of the persisted save and round-trips.
findings.detail: serialize() writes runtime.getAutomationSnapshot() (RuntimeSerializer.ts:44) but the sole load path hydrateRuntime() never calls setAutomationSnapshot, so the snapshot is silently discarded on every load and automation state does not round-trip.

adjudication.notes: serialize() writes runtime.getAutomationSnapshot() (RuntimeSerializer.ts:44) but hydrateRuntime() never calls setAutomationSnapshot (which exists and is used only in the live tick, runtimeCoreTick.ts:49), so the automation snapshot is silently discarded on every load.

findings.title: footgun: SerializedPhysicsBody.velocity and the code path body.position.x - body.prevPosition.x read as a physical velocity in units per second.
findings.detail: It is a per-tick position delta (Verlet integration), not a units/second velocity; syncPhysicsBody consumes it by reconstructing prevPosition = position - velocity, and it is intentionally never assigned to the body's separate optional velocity field (which the integrator treats as a one-shot units/second seed). Treating this delta as a real velocity elsewhere would be scaled by the tick rate.

adjudication.notes: The serialized `velocity` is indeed a per-tick Verlet position delta, not units/second, but serializePhysicsBody and syncPhysicsBody are internally consistent (reconstruct prevPosition = position - delta) and it is never assigned to body.velocity, so within the repo it round-trips correctly; this is a naming caveat with no actual defect.

findings.title: footgun: 'cat' claims to 'Display file contents' for any file and the fs layer treats .cvs as a supported semantic file stored as text.
findings.detail: vfs.readFile returns ModuleCartridge|null and discards any string value (FileSystem.base.ts:57 requires typeof!=='string', line 66 returns null for disk text), so `cat <file>.cvs` always reports 'not found' even when the .cvs file exists in the VFS. cat can never show a .cvs (text) file.

adjudication.notes: catCommand.ts:14 calls vfs.readFile, which (FileSystem.base.ts:57,66) returns null for any string-valued entry; .cvs templates are stored as strings (makeCommands.ts:63), so cat always reports a real .cvs file as 'not found'. readText exists but is not used here.

findings.title: footgun: 'rm' confirms existence with `const exists = await vfs.readFile(filename)` before deleting, implying it works for any file.
findings.detail: vfs.readFile returns null for text (.cvs) files (FileSystem.base.ts:66), so `rm <file>.cvs` returns 'File not found' and refuses to delete a .cvs file that actually exists in the VFS.

adjudication.notes: rmCommand.ts:16 uses vfs.readFile for its existence check; since readFile returns null for string (.cvs) files, rm reports 'File not found' and refuses to delete an existing .cvs entry.

findings.title: footgun: Success message 'Successfully saved to source' and description 'Dump a VFS file to disk' present save as a generally-available persistence action.
findings.detail: vfs.saveToDisk POSTs to the /__editor/save dev middleware and reads via getDiskWritePath; that endpoint only exists under the Vite dev editor plugin. In a production build the fetch hits a non-existent route and save throws / fails; the operation is dev-only, not a real 'save to source'.

adjudication.notes: saveToDisk -> saveJsonToDisk -> postJsonToEditor POSTs to /__editor/save (fileSystemBaseDisk.ts:53), a dev-only Vite editor route, so the 'saved to source' success is dev-only; the command description does mention 'editor middleware', limiting the footgun to the success message overclaiming.

findings.title: footgun: handleMakeFile builds a `.cvs` template as the string '# Cave script\n' (line 63) and writes it, and the value is cast `template as ModuleCartridge`.
findings.detail: vfs.writeFile is typed for ModuleCartridge objects; the .cvs string is persisted, but because readFile never returns strings, the just-created .cvs file is subsequently invisible to cat/rm and is dropped by fs-save. The `as ModuleCartridge` cast hides that a string is being stored under an object-typed API.

adjudication.notes: makeCommands.ts:63 builds the .cvs template as the string '# Cave script\n' and line 107 writes it via writeFile(path, template as ModuleCartridge); because readFile never returns strings, the just-created .cvs is invisible to cat/rm and dropped by fs-save, and the cast masks storing a string under an object-typed API.

findings.title: footgun: smartPathUtils imports getFileSuggestions from ./fileUtils (line 2) and getMultipartSuggestions appears to delegate depth-0 completion to it.
findings.detail: A local function getFileSuggestions(token, context) is declared at line 110 and shadows the import; the fileUtils import is unused, and the local one takes (string, context) whereas the imported one takes (string[]). The imported symbol is dead and the two same-named functions have incompatible signatures.

adjudication.notes: The claim's premise is wrong: smartPathUtils.ts:2 imports fileCache (which is used at line 115), not getFileSuggestions, from ./fileUtils. There is no imported getFileSuggestions symbol being shadowed and no unused fileUtils import; the local getFileSuggestions at line 110 shadows nothing.

findings.title: footgun: projectRoots() derives project roots by scanning fileCache for manifest paths.
findings.detail: fileCache is populated by refreshFileCache which strips /.cave-dir directory markers but keeps 'manifest.json' entries; however fileCache is only asynchronously refreshed and is clobbered with raw, unfiltered keys by `ls` (lsCommand.ts:14), so project-load/create autocomplete silently reflects a stale or marker-polluted view depending on prior commands.

adjudication.notes: projectRoots (line 5-12) keeps only paths ending in '/manifest.json', so .cave-dir markers cannot pollute project suggestions; ls does clobber fileCache with raw keys (lsCommand.ts:14) making it stale, but this only affects autocomplete and cannot affect behavior.

findings.title: footgun: scan(glob) with a parameter named `glob` implies standard glob semantics where `*` matches within a single path segment and does not cross `/`.
findings.detail: The glob is compiled to an anchored, case-insensitive regex where `*` becomes `.*`, which crosses `/` boundaries. So scan("src/*.json") also matches deeply-nested keys like src/a/b.json, and matching is case-insensitive. Same behavior in the batch path (indexedDbBatch.ts scan, line 79).

adjudication.notes: FileSystem.ts:62 compiles glob to an anchored case-insensitive regex where '*' becomes '.*' (line 71) with the 'i' flag (line 76), so '.*' crosses '/' and scan('src/*.json') over-matches nested keys like src/a/b.json; the batch path in indexedDbBatch.ts (line 69-70, 79) behaves identically. Name 'glob' implies segment-bounded, case-sensitive semantics it does not provide.

findings.title: footgun: Doc comment says "Compare two semantic version strings (e.g. \"1.0.0\" vs \"1.0.1\")", implying real semver comparison.
findings.detail: It only parses dot-separated numeric components with `Number(p) || 0`. Pre-release/build suffixes are not handled: "1.0.0-beta" parses its third component as Number("0-beta")=NaN→0, so "1.0.0-beta" compares equal to "1.0.0"; any non-numeric component silently degrades to 0, and "1.2" vs "1.2.0" are treated as equal (not newer). Drives hydration overwrite decisions (bootstrapHydration.ts:43) and bootstrap manifest selection.

adjudication.notes: version.ts:6-7 parse dot components with Number(p)||0, so '1.0.0-beta' yields Number('0-beta')=NaN->0 and compares equal to '1.0.0', and '1.2' equals '1.2.0'; the doc comment claims real semver comparison. Feeds the overwrite_db_with_disk decision at bootstrapHydration.ts:43, so a pre-release-vs-release tie silently keeps the wrong cartridge.

findings.title: footgun: assertValidBootstrapSnapshot is named as if it validates that the data is a valid bootstrap snapshot (i.e. a map of file paths to cartridges).
findings.detail: It only asserts the value is a non-null, non-array plain object that is JSON-serializable. It does not validate keys as paths or values as ModuleCartridge shape, so arbitrary object payloads pass and are later written verbatim into the store by importAll.

adjudication.notes: bootstrapSnapshot.ts:18-30 only asserts a non-null, non-array, JSON-serializable object; it never validates keys as paths or values as ModuleCartridge shape. This is the function importAll and importState actually invoke (re-exported via bootstrap.ts:11), so arbitrary object payloads pass and are written verbatim, contrary to the 'assertValidBootstrapSnapshot' name.

findings.title: footgun: `assertValidProjectModules` — the name promises it asserts every listed module is valid and rejects otherwise.
findings.detail: A non-semantic module that fails `ModuleCartridgeSchema` makes `parseProjectModuleFile` return null (projectModuleParsing.ts:25), which the try/catch does not catch; line 95 `if (module)` then silently skips it, so an invalid module is dropped from the returned map without any error. It only throws for a missing file (line 88) or a thrown ZodError.

adjudication.notes: parseProjectModuleFile (projectModuleParsing.ts:25) returns null (not a thrown ZodError) when a non-semantic module fails ModuleCartridgeSchema; the try/catch at lines 90-94 does not catch that, and line 95 `if (module)` silently drops it, so an invalid module is omitted from the returned map without error. Name promises rejection; code silently skips.

findings.title: footgun: `for (const [path, mod] of pending.entries())` then `writeModule(path, ...)` — the variable named `path` reads like a resolved absolute file path.
findings.detail: `pending` is keyed by `nextFile`, a project-relative filename (set at line 51), and `writeModule`'s parameter is `filename`. The value is a relative name, not a path; `writeModule` itself resolves it via resolveProjectFile. The name contradicts what it holds.

adjudication.notes: pending is keyed by nextFile, a project-relative filename (line 51), yet the loop binds it to a variable named `path`; writeModule's parameter is `filename` and resolves it via resolveProjectFile. Genuine name/reality mismatch but benign since the value is a valid relative filename and resolution is correct.

findings.title: footgun: `stageProjectVersion(manifestPath, currentManifestVersion, changeKind)` reads like a pure function of its arguments.
findings.detail: It reads and mutates the module-level `stagedVersions` Map (process-global singleton). The `currentManifestVersion` argument is ignored on every call after the first for a given path — subsequent bumps are computed from the cached `baseVersion`, not the passed-in version, so passing an updated current version has no effect once a bump is staged.

adjudication.notes: stageProjectVersion reads/mutates the module-level stagedVersions Map, and once an entry exists (lines 43-47) subsequent bumps recompute from staged.baseVersion, ignoring the passed-in currentManifestVersion. Signature reads pure but is stateful and drops the arg after the first call, as claimed.

findings.title: InstantTransferHandler reimplements creditResources instead of reusing the shared one
findings.detail: creditResources and ensureStateRecord here duplicate the semantics of transferResources.ts creditResources (lines 93-125), which the file already imports debitResources from. The two copies have already drifted (error strings 'Transfer failed:' vs 'Credit skipped:'), so a future fix to credit rules must be made in two places or the balancing path will diverge from the runtime path.

adjudication.notes: InstantTransferHandler lines 10-51 duplicate ensureStateRecord/creditResources from transferResources.ts lines 93-125 (the file imports debitResources from transferUtils but not creditResources), and they have already drifted in log strings ('Transfer failed:' vs 'Credit skipped:'). Real duplication/divergence; low severity as only log text differs today.

findings.title: Self-transfer bypasses the allowDeposit lock
findings.detail: findBlockedDeposit is only consulted when source.id !== target.id, so a transfer whose source and target are the same entity can credit a resource marked allowDeposit:false. If any code issues self-targeted transfers, deposit locks are silently ineffective for them.

adjudication.notes: Line 89 guards findBlockedDeposit with source.id !== target.id, so a self-targeted transfer skips the allowDeposit lock. The bypass genuinely exists; contingent on self-targeted transfers being issued, hence low.

findings.title: Scanner iterates behavior-rule actions as untyped `any`
findings.detail: action is typed `any`, so action.type/action.value/action.target are unchecked. A schema change to actions (renamed field, non-numeric value shape) would not be caught by the compiler and would silently drop or misclassify behavior levers.

adjudication.notes: action is typed 'any' at line 86, but runtime is guarded (action?.type !== 'MUTATE' return; isNumber(action.value) return), so behavior is safe today. The concern is compile-time type hygiene only and cannot affect current behavior.

findings.title: initializeWorldState silently no-ops when world blueprint/entity is absent
findings.detail: If the sys_world blueprint lacks components.state, or no sys_world entity exists, the function returns without initializing world state or the worldSeed, so the simulation runs against whatever default state existed with no signal that world configuration was skipped.

adjudication.notes: Lines 42-44 return early with no log when worldBlueprint.components.state is absent or no sys_world entity exists, so world state and worldSeed are left uninitialized with no signal. Real diagnostics gap; low severity.

findings.title: Assignment one-off installs a GC rule whose trigger it never fires
findings.detail: For a one-off assignment without a cycle ability, the pushed sys_cycle_gc rule is gated on is_depleted==1, but the assignment path only seeds is_depleted to 0 and nothing sets it to 1 (only the cycle reset rule in cycleCompiler.rules.ts flips it). The entity is therefore never garbage-collected on depletion unless a cycle ability is also present, so a one-off-only assignment silently leaks.

adjudication.notes: The premise 'nothing sets is_depleted to 1 (only the cycle reset rule)' is contradicted by the runtime: markAssignmentNodeDepleted (processingFinalization/absorptionBatchFinalization) sets state.is_depleted.value=1 when a body finishes processing at the station, and the one-off assignment compiler seeds is_depleted to 0 so its `if (state.is_depleted)` guard passes. The GC trigger therefore does fire for one-off-only assignments.

findings.title: Conditional-activation config silently dropped when a gate fails to compile
findings.detail: compileConditionalActivationConfig does `if (!onGate || !offGate) return;` with no warning, so if the structured conditions fail to produce both gates the entire config (its active-state key and both on/off rules) is emitted as nothing. Any ability targeting that conditional-activation slot then references an active-state flag that is never toggled, and the misconfiguration produces no diagnostic.

adjudication.notes: The `if (!onGate || !offGate) return;` at line 29 is unreachable as a drop path: line 26 already returns when conditions is empty, and compileStructuredConditionAllGate/NotAllGate return null only for empty conditions. With conditions non-empty both gates are always non-null, so the described silent config drop cannot occur.

findings.title: appendRuleConditions drops a malformed gate, leaving the rule ungated
findings.detail: A single unparseable condition string is skipped while its sibling gates and the rule's actions are kept, so a rule that was meant to be gated compiles to one that fires unconditionally (fail-open). The only signal is a console.warn; the compiled blueprint is silently more permissive than authored.

adjudication.notes: On a failed compileConditionText the code only console.warns and skips pushing that gate while keeping sibling gates and the rule's actions, so an authored-but-unparseable gate silently downgrades the rule to fire more permissively (fail-open). Confirmed at lines 14-26.

findings.title: toRefPath returns undefined for 5 of 9 condition kinds with no compile-time guard

findings.title: scalableCompiler seeds initial state value only when no per-body scaling is configured
findings.detail: `setInitialValue` (which writes `components.state[key].value|max`) runs only in the no-scaling branch; when perBody/multPerBody scaling is present the initial static field is left untouched and the value is expected to be produced by passiveEffects at runtime. Genuine asymmetry, narrow: a SET-to-base passive effect still runs, so the exposure is limited to callers that read the static field before passive-effect evaluation.

findings.title: Array-valued config sections are overwritten, not accumulated, across semantic files
findings.detail: When multiple .cave files each contribute array config (conditions, guidances, tutorials, knowledge), deepMergeObjects replaces the array wholesale, so all but the last file's entries are silently lost even though multi-file merge is the linker's purpose.

Since multi-file merge is the linker's stated purpose, entries from all but the last contributing file are silently lost.

findings.title: Explicit bare blueprint ids bypass namespacing and silently override across files
findings.detail: namespaceBlueprints keeps an explicit non-namespaced id as-is, and mergeRegistry only fires a debug callback on collision before overwriting; two files defining the same explicit id produce a silent last-wins override with no error and no user-visible warning.

findings.title: normalizeBpInput discards sibling blueprints when a top-level id and a blueprints wrapper coexist
findings.detail: If a .bp file has both a top-level `id` and a `blueprints` map, only the entry matching `raw.id` (or the first entry) is kept and re-keyed; any other blueprints in the wrapper are dropped without error, so authored blueprints can vanish from the cartridge.

findings.title: validatePayload never checks draftPool ids, so payloads referencing pools are flagged as broken refs
findings.detail: existingIds is built only from blueprint headers and draftOptions; a fully-qualified reference to a valid draftPool id is not in the set and is reported as a broken reference, failing an otherwise-valid save.

The draftOptions-included / draftPools-excluded asymmetry is real.

findings.title: CompilerService leaves the internal _editor block on compiled blueprints stored in the cartridge
findings.detail: compile() returns the draft with _editor intact (it only early-returns when _editor is absent), so RuntimeCartridge.blueprints carry authoring-only _editor data that BlueprintV2 does not declare; downstream consumers see undeclared extra state and serialization has to special-case stripping it.

Real leakage of authoring state into the runtime cartridge; low impact.

findings.title: Compiler ignores operator precedence; mixed arithmetic/boolean folds strictly left-to-right
findings.detail: The token loop applies every op/keyword in source order with no precedence, so `1 + 2 * 3` compiles to *(+(1,2),3)=9 not 7, and `a AND b OR c` compiles to or(and(a,b),c) regardless of intended grouping. Any rule authored assuming standard precedence silently evaluates to the wrong number/boolean.

Tokens are produced by plain whitespace-splitting (logicTokenService.parseTokensFromInput) with no precedence structure, and this compiler is the sole grammar, so rules authored assuming standard precedence silently evaluate to wrong numbers/booleans.

findings.title: Tier-2 isolation is enforced on QUERY/SLOT but not on by-id entity access
findings.detail: createLogicDataFacade resolves any unknown top-level var name as an entity id via snapshot.getEntity in ALL modes. json-logic's `var` walks the first path segment, so tier2_entity logic — explicitly blocked from QUERY/QUERY_COUNT (ops.ts:19,33) — can still read arbitrary entities and their fields with `{var:"<entityId>.<field>"}`, defeating the intended tier-2 sandbox.

adjudication.notes: createLogicDataFacade (line 30) resolves any unknown top-level var as an entity id via context.snapshot.getEntity with NO mode check, while QUERY/QUERY_COUNT throw for tier2_entity (ops.ts:19,33). json-logic-js var splits on '.' and walks the first segment against data, so tier2 rules can read arbitrary entities/fields via {var:'<entityId>.<field>'}. findings.title: Operator right-hand operand cannot be NOT or a sub-expression
findings.detail: For an `op` token the RHS is read with tokenToAtom(requireToken(index)) rather than consumeAtom(), so `x == NOT y` throws LogicCompileError('Unexpected token keyword') even though NOT is accepted as an AND/OR operand and at expression start. The grammar is asymmetric and rejects otherwise-reasonable comparisons against a negated value.

adjudication.notes: For an op token the RHS is read via tokenToAtom(requireToken(index)) at line 90, which only handles 'val'/'ref' and throws "Unexpected token 'keyword'" for NOT — whereas NOT is accepted at expression start and as an AND/OR operand via consumeAtom (line 58). So 'x == NOT y' throws while the negation is legal elsewhere; the grammar is asymmetric and rejects comparisons against a negated value.

findings.title: Shared EMPTY_SELF singleton used as default self target
findings.detail: A single module-level EMPTY_SELF = {} is reused as the Proxy target for every evaluation whose context.self is nullish. The facade is read-only today so this is benign, but any future write through the self facade (or a json-logic op mutating `this`) would leak state across unrelated evaluations. It also has no id, so assignmentMap lookups collapse to assignmentMap[''].

adjudication.notes: EMPTY_SELF = {} (line 12) is a shared module-level object reused as the facade target when context.self is nullish, and having no id it makes assignmentMap lookups collapse to assignmentMap[''] (createEntityFacade uses target.id ?? ''). The claim is accurate, but the facade is read-only so no state leaks and self.assignment still yields {parentId:null} correctly — the finder itself notes it is benign today; no current behavioral defect.

findings.title: Stale node-overlay bounds retained when a pretty transfer glyph shrinks out of view
findings.detail: createNodeOverlayDisplayBoundsFromRadius returns null when the resolved radius is <= 0 (radius can collapse as payload/scale drops), and the `if (bounds)` guard then leaves tickCtx.scratch.nodeOverlayDisplayBounds pointing at the previous frame's bounds instead of clearing it. Overlays/hit-testing that key off these bounds keep targeting a location the glyph no longer occupies. findings.title: Simplex permutation cache grows unbounded across many seeds
findings.detail: getPerm memoizes a 512-byte Uint8Array per distinct seed in a module-level Map that is never cleared or size-capped. compileVeinGuidePath calls createSimplex2D(edge.seed) and edge seeds vary per edge/regeneration, so over a long session with many distinct vein seeds the cache accumulates entries for the lifetime of the module, a slow memory leak.

findings.title: Unbounded wave-phase accumulation for nervous veins
findings.detail: advanceWavePhase decrements state.wavePhaseRad every frame with no modulo/wrap. Over a long-running scene the magnitude grows without bound; once it is large the value fed into Math.sin (veinsRopePath.ts:88-93) loses floating-point precision, so the animated waviness of long-lived nervous veins can visibly quantize or jitter. Also forces a full-path recompute every frame (veinsEdgeTick.ts:63-66) because fullPathResolvedForPhaseRad never re-matches.

adjudication.notes: advanceWavePhase decrements state.wavePhaseRad every frame with no modulo/wrap (lines 13-20), so magnitude grows unbounded for long-lived nervous veins and eventually loses float precision when fed to Math.sin. The forced per-frame recompute is largely inherent to animation; the precision degradation is real but only at extreme runtimes.

findings.title: Spawn loop relies on spawnPulse always pushing to avoid a hang
findings.detail: Inside `while (state.spawnCarry >= 1)`, spawnCarry is only decremented after a successful spawn; the `const pulse = state.pulses.at(-1); if (!pulse) continue;` path loops back without decrementing spawnCarry or advancing the ordinal. It is safe only because spawnPulse unconditionally pushes, so .at(-1) is never undefined. If spawnPulse ever early-returns (e.g. pool exhaustion added later), this becomes an infinite loop that freezes the frame.

adjudication.notes: Inside while(spawnCarry >= 1), the `const pulse = state.pulses.at(-1); if (!pulse) continue;` path loops back without decrementing spawnCarry or advancing the ordinal. It is safe only because spawnPulse unconditionally pushes (veinsPulseLifecycle.ts:42); if spawnPulse ever early-returns this becomes an infinite loop. Latent, does not manifest today.

findings.title: Producer-resource light picked by a fragile duck-typing score
findings.detail: readProducerResource chooses the light color by scoring each state entry on ad-hoc shape heuristics (allowWithdraw/allowDeposit/visible/max presence) rather than an explicit resource marker. Ties resolve to the first-seen key via Object.entries order, and any change to state-entry shape silently reassigns which resource color a node shows, with no error. Latent correctness/coupling risk in the vein/producer visuals.

adjudication.notes: readProducerResource scores state entries (restricted to keys in PRODUCER_LIGHTS) by ad-hoc shape heuristics (allowWithdraw/allowDeposit/visible/max), and ties resolve to the first-seen key via strict > and Object.entries order. Any change to state-entry shape could silently reassign the resource color; latent coupling risk, only bites when multiple producer keys coexist.

findings.title: Distress non-physics path makes root/overlay anchor visible with no inverse on recovery
findings.detail: When distress becomes active the tick calls scratch.root.setVisible(true), overlayAnchor.setPosition(target.x,target.y) and overlayAnchor.setVisible(true). On recovery (ratio >= DISTRESS_THRESHOLD) or loss of body/target it calls hideHalos(), which only kills tweens and hides the three halo images (distressHaloHelpers.hideDistressHalos); it never restores overlayAnchor visibility/position or the root visibility. The entity's overlay anchor is left visible and repositioned, and root is left force-shown, leaking distress state into later frames.

adjudication.notes: On active distress the tick force-shows scratch.root and repositions/shows overlayAnchor (lines 89-91), but hideHalos() only kills tweens and hides the three halo images; it never restores overlayAnchor visibility/position or root visibility, so distress state can leak into later frames after recovery or loss of target.

findings.title: Progress-bar slot count is a magic 4 duplicating RESOURCE_PROGRESS_BAR_POSITIONS length
findings.detail: createProgressBarSlots hardcodes Array.from({ length: 4 }), while tickProgressBars iterates RESOURCE_PROGRESS_BAR_POSITIONS (currently 4 entries) and indexes input.slots[index]. The invariant that these two counts match is unenforced: adding a 5th position to the constant makes slots[4] undefined, so hideProgressBarSlot(undefined) / tickActiveProgressBarSlot with an undefined slot throws at runtime.

adjudication.notes: createProgressBarSlots hardcodes Array.from({length:4}) while progressBarTick.ts:34-35 iterates RESOURCE_PROGRESS_BAR_POSITIONS (currently 4) and indexes slots[index] with no undefined guard. The count invariant is unenforced: a 5th position makes slots[4] undefined and hideProgressBarSlot(undefined) throws. Latent, requires editing the constant.

findings.title: Glyph pulse delay lookup can index past delayMsByPosition and propagate NaN
findings.detail: readPulseValue computes ctx.timeMs - glyph.pulse.delayMsByPosition[placement.position]. GlyphPlacement.position is typed 0..8 but GlyphPulseConfig.delayMsByPosition is an unbounded number[] with no length guarantee. If a cartridge supplies a placement whose position exceeds the delay array length, the lookup is undefined, timeMs - undefined is NaN, and getDemandPulse(entityId, NaN) returns NaN (clampPulse(NaN,0,1) === NaN). That NaN survives clamp01 in resolveGlyphPlacementRenderModel and flows into the glyph transform (position/scale/rotation), silently corrupting rendering with no error.

adjudication.notes: The NaN premise is contradicted by the Zod schema: glyphs.ts validates position with z.number().int().min(0).max(8) and delayMsByPosition with z.array(...).length(9), so position 0..8 always indexes into a length-9 array for schema-valid cartridges. The TS type number[] looks loose but the runtime schema guarantees the length, so the out-of-bounds/NaN path cannot occur.

findings.title: AvatarGlyphModule restores scratch.mainImage AFTER destroying the wrapped glyph module
findings.detail: destroy() calls runtime.destroy(...) (glyphModuleRuntime.destroyGlyphImages sets scratch.mainImage = null and releases the glyph images) and then unconditionally reassigns dCtx.scratch.mainImage = preservedMain, the silhouette captured at create time. If the AvatarModule that owned that silhouette has already been destroyed (which nulls mainImage and releases the silhouette to the pool), this writes a released/stale image reference back into scratch.mainImage, defeating the null-out and creating a dangling pooled-object reference dependent on module destroy order.

adjudication.notes: destroy() calls runtime.destroy (glyphModuleRuntime.destroyGlyphImages sets scratch.mainImage=null) then unconditionally reassigns dCtx.scratch.mainImage = preservedMain (line 44). If the AvatarModule that owned that silhouette was already destroyed and released it to the pool, this writes a stale/released reference back, defeating the null-out; order-dependent dangling reference.

findings.title: star6 core/fill glyph is not a symmetric 6-point star
findings.detail: The 'star6' case builds two triangles via starPoints(3, outer) (inner radius passed equal to the outer radius, so the points are not a true star) and mirrors the second with `128 - point.y + 10` — an asymmetric +10px vertical offset. The rendered star6 is lopsided and does not match the geometry of the stroke-path drawStar6, producing an off-center/asymmetric glyph texture.

Since star6 is in normalizeThickness's ignore-set and the core path is tried first (returns true), this asymmetric texture is what actually renders.

findings.title: Dead draw-function modules diverge from the live rendering path
findings.detail: glyphShapeDrawFns.ts has no importers, and glyphShapeDrawFnsRings.ts contributes only its size constant. These modules define an entire alternate set of shape geometries (e.g. drawStar6 as a Star of David, T=6/10 stroke widths) that no longer render anything. These define an alternate shape set (e.g. drawStar6 as a symmetric Star of David, T=10) that renders nothing; they present as the shape source of truth but are dead and diverge from the live core/stroke paths.

findings.title: Preset epoch check keyed on object reference identity
findings.detail: syncEpoch compares `presetsRaw === this.lastPresetsRaw` by reference. A caller that rebuilds an equal-but-new preset object each frame forces a full parsePresets + cache.clear + ordinal reset every call (re-validating every preset and discarding all procedural allocations), while a caller that mutates the same object in place is never picked up. Correctness and cost both hinge on an unstated referential-stability contract.

Latent contract issue; current caller passes the stable cartridge object so no active break, hence low.

findings.title: Procedural glyph capacity throws instead of degrading
findings.detail: findNextAvailableOrdinal throws once nextOrdinal reaches MAX_GLYPH_CAPACITY (4^9) with no reserved-signature slots left. Because get() -> allocateProcedural is on the render/resolve path, an exhausted registry turns a request for an unknown display_key into a thrown error that can break the frame rather than falling back to a placeholder glyph.

adjudication.notes: findNextAvailableOrdinal throws at line 111 on exhaustion, and get()->allocateProcedural is on the resolve path, so an exhausted registry throws rather than degrading. Requires ~4^9 distinct procedural keys to reach, so realistically unreachable; real but low.

findings.title: exhaustionLogged flag is a dead store; capacity-exhaustion warning spams every call
findings.detail: The `if (!this.exhaustionLogged)` block only sets the flag and contains no logging; the console.warn sits AFTER the block and fires unconditionally on every get() once variants are exhausted, flooding the console per-entity per-key instead of once. The guarded flag is never read to suppress anything.

findings.title: Tick context shallow-clones the entity every frame when attention light is suppressed
findings.detail: resolveTickEntity returns `{...entity, __attentionLightSuppressed:true}` — a fresh object identity each tick for every non-focused entity during tutorial/announcement focus. Any downstream display module keyed on entity reference identity sees a new object every frame (breaking identity caches), plus a per-entity per-frame allocation.

findings.title: Empty-string entity id collides all id-less entities into one structural record
findings.detail: syncFullRebuild uses `entity.id ?? ''` as the map key; two or more entities lacking an id all map to key '' , so they overwrite each other in the records map and only one gets a visual instance. The same '' also becomes the DisplaySpec.entityId downstream.

findings.title: Structural incremental sync ignores mutationRevision when a full-rebuild trigger also changed
findings.detail: The `else if (syncState.mutationRevision !== mutationRevision)` only runs when fullRebuild is false. On the same tick that a full rebuild fires, syncState.mutationRevision is overwritten by Object.assign without the changed-entity pass running; this is benign only if a full rebuild always supersedes per-entity mutations, which is an unstated assumption.

findings.title: getAvatarPart indexes catalogs but callers pass unvalidated appearance indices
findings.detail: generateAvatar*Texture pass appearance.faceShapeIndex/hairShapeIndex/eyeShapeIndex straight into getAvatarPart, which throws on an out-of-range index. Because assertAvatarAppearance (called first) never checks these indices, a corrupted-but-keyed appearance throws inside texture generation rather than being caught at the guard.

findings.title: Unknown/future visual-event kinds silently become smoke puffs
findings.detail: The dispatcher has no default/reject branch: any event whose kind is not one of the four explicitly handled cases falls through to spawnSmokePuff(scene, layers, textureManager, event.x, event.y, event.radius). A newly added event kind (or any variant lacking x/y/radius) would spawn an unintended smoke puff at undefined coordinates instead of being ignored or flagged. Correct today only because kill_smoke_puff happens to want a puff.

findings.title: Nervous veins render permanently static (no flow blobs)

findings.title: Dead base-width computation in the display builder

findings.title: Terminal-target resolution is O(n^2) over the edge list

findings.title: resolveBodyAvatarExportInputs is dead production code
findings.detail: The exported function has no non-test importer anywhere in src/ (only its own .test.ts references it); the live avatar path uses buildBodyAvatarImageRequest instead.
